subject: Proportional exposure crediting + spot-burst insurance

Subject: Helio RFP - pricing construct question

Hi Rishi,

Thanks again for taking our RFP. Two quick follow-ups from procurement on the commercial schedule:

1) We want a billing mechanism that protects Helio from short-term spikes from batch workloads while providing Redwood predictable revenue. Procurement called this an "exposure-mitigated" crediting structure. Can you outline a proposal that avoids heavy-handed multi-year gross-commits but still gives us volume price progressivity?

2) For seasonal analytics bursts (up to 7x baseline for 48 hours), would you support a short-duration "spot-burst insurance" add-on that caps marginal rates and returns a portion of spend as credits if bursts exceed pre-agreed thresholds? If so, what pricing leverages would you propose (e.g., daily caps, multiplier bands)?

We're attaching the relevant RFP pricing worksheet for context. Please send a short proposed amendment we can show procurement by EOD Thursday.

Best,
Jon

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Helio RFP - pricing construct question

Jon — thanks for the clear ask and the worksheet. High-level response below; attaching a two-pager and a price sketch.

Summary proposal (short):
- Anchored annualized credits: Helio commits to an annualized baseline (e.g., 100M tokens/month equivalent) but we amortize that as monthly drawdown credits rather than strict upfront consumption. This reduces churn pressure while preserving discount progressivity.
- Proportional exposure crediting: rather than hard tiers, credits scale proportionally with rolling-30d usage vs baseline; overages are billed but partially credited back at month-end based on agreed smoothing parameters (protects Helio from single-day spikes).
- Spot-burst insurance add-on: fixed monthly insurance fee (small percent of committed spend) that provides a capped marginal rate during covered bursts and a partial refund/credit for burst spend above the burst cap.

Concrete levers we recommend to include in the contract (sketch):
- Baseline: set Annual Committed Tokens (ACT). Monthly credits = ACT/12.
- Rolling smoothing window: 30 days; if monthly consumption > credits by X%, overage billed at standard overage rate but 40% of that overage converts into a credit pool applied the next month (configurable 20–60%).
- Spot-burst insurance: tiered product. Example:
  * Bronze: $5k/mo + burst cap multiplier 3x baseline/day, marginal overage capped at $0.015/token (instead of $0.025), 25% refunds to credit pool for amount beyond cap.
  * Silver: $12k/mo + 5x multiplier, marginal overage capped at $0.012/token, 40% refunds to credit pool.
  * Gold: $25k/mo + 7x multiplier, marginal overage capped at $0.009/token, 60% refunds.

Operational guardrails: can limit insurance to pre-registered endpoints/models, require a minimal 48-hour notice for scheduled large backfills to avoid surprise classification, and provide real-time billing alerts.

I'll loop in Marissa and Ben to refine numbers. Attached: Redwood-pricing-breakdown.pdf and a stubbed spreadsheet with example math.

Quick question: do you want the crediting to be automatic (applied to invoice) or returned as a one-time monthly credit note? We can do either.

Thanks — will follow with an internal note that includes alternate credit percentages and the net ARR impact for Redwood.

Best,
Rishi

Please reply with: 1) suggested credit % to propose, 2) recommended insurance monthly fee and marginal cap levels, and 3) whether we require invoice crediting vs credit note (financial ops preference?).

Thanks — R

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>

Date: Wed, 02 Sep 2026 11:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Helio RFP - pricing construct question

Rishi / Ben — quick notes: 
1) Credit %: propose 35% (midpoint between 20/40). It balances customer protection and ARR predictability. If Helio signs multi-year, push to 45%.
2) Insurance monthly fee: recommend Bronze $6k / Silver $13k / Gold $28k (round up vs your sketch to preserve margin).
3) Marginal caps: bump Bronze cap to $0.016 (slightly higher), Silver $0.011, Gold $0.009 (agree).
4) Financial ops: invoice crediting preferred for customer UX; notes complicate P&L and collections. If procurement insists on notes, Finance will accept but will need a monthly reconciliation workflow.

Also flag: require a clause that scheduled high-volume backfills (>24h) need 48h notice to qualify for insurance — otherwise we call them "unregistered bursts" and bill standard overage.

Happy to draft the legal pricing appendix language for Helio if you want.

-Marissa
VP Commercial Operations
marissa.cole@redwood.com

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>

Thanks — my commercial read: Helio is trying to avoid a large committed ARR number while preserving progressive economics. If they want limited downside protection, Silver is the clean compromise. A couple of tweak suggestions: 

- Make the credit pool auto-apply but cap total monthly refunds at 15% of monthly invoice to avoid churnable credits. Helio gets smoothing but can't repeatedly drive negative AR.
- For Gold, require 12-month minimum term for the insurance add-on so the economics are preserved.
- Add an "exhaustion" definition: if credits fall below 50% of monthly baseline three months in a row, we reserve right to re-evaluate tiering/pricing at renewal.

If you want, I can draft the short contract appendix and annotate with expected net ARR impact per tier.

—Ben

Jon / Marta — thanks for the quick turn. Per your request, attached is a concise commercial appendix that operationalizes the three levers we discussed: anchored annualized credits, proportional exposure crediting, and a 3-tier spot-burst insurance add-on. Highlights:

- Baseline AR: Annual Committed Tokens (ACT) amortized monthly.
- Rolling smoothing: 30-day rolling window; overage refunds converted to credit pool at 35% by default (Helio can choose 20/35/45).
- Spot-burst insurance: Bronze/Silver/Gold as proposed — monthly fees Bronze $6k / Silver $13k / Gold $28k; marginal overage caps Bronze $0.016 / Silver $0.011 / Gold $0.009.
- Operational items: pre-registered endpoints, 48-hour notice for scheduled large backfills, real-time billing alerts, monthly invoice crediting (preferred).

I've attached the wording as a short appendix and a worked example of the math using your worksheet. If this looks good, we can: 1) convert the appendix into an addendum for the main SOW, and 2) prepare a DocuSign-ready signature block.

Would you like us to share an impact table that shows projected monthly cashflow, credit pool draw rates, and modeled ARR under Bronze/Silver/Gold? Happy to run that next.

Thanks — Rishi
